title: Before the next idea
author: Laura Burke
summary: Primary teacher Laura Burke reflects on the knowing-doing gap in professional learning, the space between understanding an approach and making it a reliable habit. Using the hinge question as an example, she argues that professional development should treat understanding as the beginning, not the endpoint. Teachers need expert modelling that makes the thinking explicit, low-stakes rehearsal with plausible pupil answers, focused feedback and another attempt. She notes we would never expect pupils to jump from explanation to independent practice, and professional learning deserves the same scaffolding. Time for this must be protected in the working week. She turns the point on herself, asking why she keeps searching for the next idea before giving the last one enough attention.
points: The knowing-doing gap is the distance between understanding an approach and putting it into everyday practice.
Professional development should move beyond explaining an approach or presenting a polished document to rehearsal and practice.
Expert modelling should show the approach and make the thinking behind it explicit, such as how to read pupil answers to a hinge question.
Teachers need low-stakes rehearsal, focused feedback and another try, with time protected within the working week.
Introducing an idea is only the beginning, and teachers should return to it and ask what is changing for pupils.
quotes: Understanding an approach should be the beginning of professional learning, not its endpoint.
It is the space between understanding an approach and putting it into practice. Bridging that gap requires energy and conscious commitment to new habits.
Expert modelling should show what the approach looks like and make the thinking behind it explicit.
We would not expect pupils to move from a clear explanation to confident independent practice without support. Our professional learning should make space for modelling, rehearsal and feedback too.
If this matters, time for it needs to be protected within the working week, rather than left for teachers to find afterwards.
Why am I looking for the next idea before giving the last one enough time and attention?
We need time to practise it, return to it and ask what is changing for pupils. The classroom has to remain the point.
